nodes.title: SG-5.1 Layer order, render context, SceneObject and buildScene
nodes.body:
Context: game/src has the layer enum (content/schema.ts), the object schema and getSceneView, but no layer ordering, render context, scene object entity or scene-building step. Desired behavior: add these as one sequenced change with no concurrent writers, so a scene is built only from content definitions into background, furniture, objects, characters, effects and ui layers. Expected result: buildScene(ctx, scene) creates one entity per content object at the depth of its layer. Why: lets future content changes add objects without touching the engine.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given the six layers, when LAYER_ORDER is read, then it equals background, furniture, objects, characters, effects, ui in that order
- Given a SceneSpec with objects on several layers, when buildScene runs, then one entity per object is created with depth ordered by layer
- Given no hardcoded object ids in engine code, when a new object is added to scene content, then buildScene creates it without code changes


## Scope
- In scope: game/src/engine layer order, render context and buildScene
- In scope: game/src/entities SceneObject
- Out of scope: Phaser scene wiring
- Out of scope: new art assets
- Out of scope: effects and transitions
- Preserve: getSceneView and performAction behavior
- Preserve: existing zod schemas


## Technical constraints
- Modules must not import phaser; the render context is an injected interface
- Reuse layerSchema, ObjectSpec and SceneSpec from game/src/content/schema.ts


## Definition of done
- All three requirements have Act and Verify units passing
- game typecheck passes


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Six-layer render order and injected render context exist
nodes.body:
Context: layerSchema lists the six layers but nothing orders them for rendering. Desired behavior: a layers module exports LAYER_ORDER and layerDepth, and a renderContext module exports RenderContext, RenderSpriteSpec and RenderHandle interfaces. Expected result: depth is monotonic in layer order and unknown layers fall back to objects. Why: gives every entity a single rendering-order source.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given LAYER_ORDER, when layerDepth is called for each layer, then depths are strictly increasing in order
- Given an undefined or unknown layer string, when layerDepth is called, then it returns the objects depth


## Scope
- In scope: layers.ts
- In scope: renderContext.ts
- Out of scope: Phaser adapter
- Preserve: layerSchema


## Technical constraints
- No phaser import


## Definition of done
- Exports typed and tested


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · SceneObject entity renders one content object and tracks visibility
nodes.body:
Context: objects carry asset, position, scale, layer and visibleWhen in content. Desired behavior: SceneObject created from an ObjectSpec and a RenderContext creates one sprite at the object's position, scale and layer depth, applies visibleWhen on sync(state), and releases the handle on destroy. Expected result: entity state follows game state. Why: objects become independently managed entities.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given an ObjectSpec, when SceneObject is constructed, then ctx.createSprite is called once with its asset key, position, scale and layer depth
- Given visibleWhen on a flag, when sync is called with the flag false then true, then the handle setVisible receives false then true
- Given a constructed entity, when destroy is called, then the handle destroy is called once


## Scope
- In scope: entities/SceneObject.ts
- Out of scope: hover and click handling
- Preserve: evaluateAll semantics


## Technical constraints
- Use evaluateAll from game/src/systems/conditions.ts
- No phaser import


## Dependencies
- REQ1


## Definition of done
- Entity tested with a fake RenderContext


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · buildScene creates all scene entities purely from content in layer order
nodes.body:
Context: scenes are defined in YAML content. Desired behavior: buildScene(ctx, scene) creates one SceneObject per scene object and returns them sorted by layer depth, grouped by layer, using no hardcoded ids. Expected result: the bedroom content yields entities across furniture and objects layers in order. Why: scene construction is data-driven.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a scene with objects on objects, furniture and background layers, when buildScene runs, then the returned list is ordered background, furniture, objects
- Given a scene, when buildScene runs, then ctx.createSprite is called exactly once per object
- Given an empty objects array, when buildScene runs, then it returns an empty result without error


## Scope
- In scope: engine/buildScene.ts
- Out of scope: asset preload
- Preserve: content schema


## Technical constraints
- Stable order within the same layer


## Dependencies
- REQ1
- REQ2


## Definition of done
- buildScene tested against fake context


## Clarifying questions
- None

sync applies visibleWhen

steps.action: Define class SceneObject with readonly spec: ObjectSpec, readonly depth, private handle. Constructor(spec, ctx) computes depth with layerDepth(spec.layer) and calls ctx.createSprite({key: spec.asset, x: spec.position.x, y: spec.position.y, scale: spec.scale, depth}). sync(state: GameState) calls handle.setVisible(evaluateAll(state, spec.visibleWhen)). destroy() calls handle.destroy().
